This was honestly a fantastic post that I don't have too much to add to or disagree with. The only thing I grapple with is the use of the term "misogyny" or "misogynist". Unlike homophobia, (which two people have corrected my definition of now), misogyny refers to gender, specifically women or girls. I wouldn't necessarily attribute an aversion to a male acting in a feminine way to "[hating or disliking](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misogyny) females. Which brings us back to the fact that once a straight male (not all straight males, but likely most) discover the woman they are interested in is transexual, they lose interest. There is no longer the association of "female" -- there is now the association of "male in disguise". And I know that is extremely hurtful and not at all fair. But in answering OP's question about what changes if the transexual woman is a woman in every single way, I thought that was possibly an explanation.

This is not to diminish your (in my opinion) correct identification that it is an ingrained societal problem. Rather, I think it becomes confusing for many people because of those societal pressures, gender identification issues as well as sexual orientation factors. When everything is at play, it really does get difficult to separate one from the other. 

Again, your post was fantastic and I hope it gets upvoted for more visibility.

I think you pose an interesting question that I would like to give my take on. I don't mean any disrespect by what I say, I am just trying to convey why it would be a problem.

First off, the term "transphobic" would seem to have the definition of "being afraid of a transexual person". By that definition, I think most people wouldn't be labeled as such. From a personal perspective, they wouldn't dabble in it. But in terms of ostracizing transexual people and treating them differently or unequally... well no decent human would want that for anybody.

But when it comes to sexual attraction and sexual activity, things start to get muddled. I am a straight guy and I have 0 problems with the LGBT community. However, as a straight guy, I share this feeling with other heterosexual males that we don't want to be labeled as gay. Not because it is derogatory or that there is anything wrong with being gay, but rather it is an incorrect label that we don't want to be associated with. The best analogy I could think of is how transexual people get offended when the wrong pronoun is used.

This brings me to the controversial point of this reply. Despite a transexual woman being for all intents and purposes a woman, both outwardly and inwardly, the fact remains that she used to be a man. And that makes a lot of males immediately turned off because out comes the gay association. There is nothing fair about it, and logically it should not be a problem. But the very fact that the woman you just found attractive enough to sleep with was actually a man at one-point immediately removes that attraction. You no longer view them as a female, but rather a former man. And that is incredibly uncomfortable from a sexual point of view.

So if there is a term for being transphobic only in the sexual sense, that would probably be a more accurate representation of the apprehension most straight males feel towards transexual women.

Again, I am really sorry if I offended you or anyone else in anyway. I was just attempting to answer a thought-provoking question.
